A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AlphaSteer, with matching core equations, experiments, and identifiable appendix content. The text, tables, equations, and figures support a reliable comparison despite substantial appendix expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original jailbreak-defense and utility experiments on three LLMs, alongside activation analyses and response case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, adaptive attacks, model-size experiments, ablations, and evaluator comparisons.

M1.justification: The principal null-space projection, regularized linear regression, and steering equations remain unchanged. Appendix E.3 adds an experimental AlphaSteer variant replacing linear regression with a two-layer MLP, a limited architectural adaptation rather than a replacement of the main method.

E1.justification: v2 adds AdvPrompter, four FlipAttack variants, and WildGuard Test with 329 unseen harmful queries (Appendix E.5). It also introduces an adaptive white-box GCG scenario with access to the steering defense (E.6), substantially extending the original attack coverage.

E2.justification: Circuit Breaker, previously only cited, becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables 1–2. Supervised refusal training is newly compared with AlphaSteer in Tables 7–9 and appears as Refusal SFT in Table 18. The original steering baselines remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include 1B/3B model configurations, data-matched refusal training, 200-step adaptive GCG, projection-energy coverage measurements, and Llama-Guard-3-8B evaluation. Appendix D.1 also adds 900 MATH training prompts to the previously stated composition while retaining the 14,000 total, an unresolved count inconsistency that does not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained activation and steering-strength analyses, v2 adds MLP substitution, math-data exclusion, benign-data-size and null-space-ratio ablations. It also examines adaptive robustness, CAST's math-trigger failure, training/test overlap, case-specific activation changes, and disagreement between evaluation models (Appendices D–G).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new coverage distributions describe activation variability, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Retained entries in Tables 1–2 have identical reported values, but v2 adds substantial new results. Examples include 95.5% DSR under adaptive GCG (Figure 7), 90 seconds versus 20 minutes for AlphaSteer and refusal training (Table 9), and utility scores falling from 67.30 to 39.43 when benign training data decrease from 14k to 1k (Table 14).

T1.justification: Appendix C adds a stepwise computational-cost derivation and training/inference complexity comparisons. The null-space equivalence lemma, projection proof, and closed-form regression derivation in Appendix B remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: learned null-space-constrained steering improves refusal while preserving benign utility. Additional experiments support this existing claim without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains utility preservation through training/test activation-space coverage and identifies deterioration with insufficient benign data or excessive null-space ratios. It adds interpretations involving possible MLP overfitting, adaptive-attack geometry, and evaluator disagreement. Section 5 replaces the unexplored-MLP/model-size limitations with larger-model and reasoning-model boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds computational pseudocode, training-time information, stronger descriptions of attack-family exclusion, an additional implementation-access address, and an LLM-use disclosure. Existing hardware, software, decoding, and principal hyperparameter disclosures remain largely unchanged; the revised benign-data description contains an unresolved total.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 now acknowledges learned steering in Guiding Giants, HyperSteer, and Activation Scaling, distinguishing AlphaSteer through principled guidance. Other safety, representation-learning, and attack references are updated, while the overall positioning around the safety–utility trade-off remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable, with local condensation and terminology edits. Existing appendices are reorganized around new material, the broader-impacts discussion becomes an ethics statement, and reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: v2 expands the main tables with Circuit Breaker rows and adds extensive appendix tables, an algorithm display, adaptive-attack plots, CAST condition distributions, coverage plots, and an evaluator-mismatch example. Most original figures survive under new numbering; the conference template also changes typography and layout.

improvement.justification: Adaptive-attack testing, stronger comparators, and coverage/null-space ablations substantially address v1's limited evidence about robustness and when utility preservation fails. Evaluator comparisons further expose measurement sensitivity. These gains outweigh reporting defects, including the inconsistent training-data total and Table 15's 3k-data average of 98.71%, which conflicts with its displayed attack rates averaging 92.14%.
